incidents.title: Metabase SQL-injection 0-day (GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf) — unauth admin takeover
incidents.summary: An unauthenticated remote attacker can inject arbitrary SQL into the Metabase application database and mint administrator access, then read connected-database credentials and export data. Exploited in the wild before a fix; n8n disclosed an attacker used it to pull 136 customer records. CVSS 10.0. Durable catch: a POST to /api/session/reset_password returning 400 immediately followed by a GET /api/user/current returning 200 — the reset-password injection signature.
incidents.action: Upgrade to a fixed build (1.58.24 / 1.59.21 / 1.60.17 / 1.61.11 / 1.62.9 / 1.63.5); if you cannot patch at once, block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint at the proxy; hunt access logs for a 400 on that endpoint immediately followed by a 200 on /api/user/current, and rotate every credential Metabase held for connected databases.

iocs.context: Metabase unauth SQL-injection → admin (no CVE assigned)
Reset-password injection signature in web logs
Exploited endpoint — block as temporary mitigation

incidents.title: CVE-2026-63077 — JetBrains TeamCity unauthenticated deserialization RCE
incidents.summary: On-prem TeamCity exposes unauthenticated RCE through the agent polling protocol: a permissive XStream allowlist adds TeamCity protocol classes without removing XStream's default permissions, so untrusted data deserializes into code execution. CISA added it to KEV (federal deadline Aug 8) and a public PoC writes .JSPWS files to run commands. CVSS 9.8. Durable catch: unexpected .JSPWS files under the TeamCity web/work directories and agent-protocol requests from hosts that are not build agents.
incidents.action: Update TeamCity to the patched build now; keep the agent protocol/port off the public internet; hunt for .JSPWS files and unexpected command execution under the TeamCity service account, and rotate CI secrets/deploy tokens if the server was exposed.

iocs.context: On-prem TeamCity — unauth deserialization RCE via agent polling protocol

iocs.value: XStream deserialization via agent polling protocol
iocs.context: Default permissions retained ahead of TeamCity allowlist
Public-PoC artifact used to execute commands

incidents.title: CVE-2026-68820 — Windows afd.sys use-after-free, SYSTEM privilege escalation
incidents.summary: A use-after-free in the Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (afd.sys), the kernel-mode backbone of the Windows Sockets API, lets a locally authenticated attacker win a race condition and elevate to SYSTEM. Exploited in the wild as a zero-day and fixed in the Aug 11 Patch Tuesday, where Microsoft shipped 421 CVE fixes. Local EoP is the pivot after initial access — patch is the fix; also close CVE-2026-62832 (publicly-disclosed User Profile Service EoP) in the same batch.
incidents.action: Deploy the August 2026 Windows updates now, prioritizing multi-user and internet-facing hosts; because the UAF is a local elevation, treat any unpatched host showing signs of initial access as high priority and pull forensics before it reaches SYSTEM.

iocs.context: afd.sys use-after-free — local elevation to SYSTEM (exploited)
User Profile Service link-following EoP — publicly disclosed, same batch
Critical DNS / TFTP / QUIC / HPC Pack RCEs patched same day — prioritize on exposed roles

incidents.title: ClickFix macOS Go stealer — DRAIN routine empties crypto wallets
incidents.summary: A fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix lure has the victim paste a Terminal command that runs a Bash profiler, which fetches an architecture-matched Mach-O Go stealer for iCloud Keychain, browser passwords and cached credentials, then a DRAIN function swaps in attacker addresses to redirect BTC/LTC/DOGE/ETH/XMR/XRP balances. Payloads sit on sanctioned Aeza Group hosting. Durable catch: the launch agent com.apple.softwareupdated.plist plus payloads staged under the trustd / homeenergyd / softwareupdate caches — none are real Apple files.
incidents.action: Block the IPs/domain below; on managed Macs hunt the four cache/LaunchAgent paths and the two Mach-O hashes; remind users that no legitimate site asks them to paste a command into Terminal.

iocs.context: Domain used in the ClickFix phase

incidents.title: QuickFox VPN supply-chain compromise — FDMTP backdoor (Mustang Panda)
incidents.summary: The QuickFox VPN Windows installer was trojanized for roughly a year (since at least Aug 2025): a modified Electron renderer HTML pulls a JavaScript loader that fingerprints the host, then side-loads FDMTP, a backdoor tied to China-nexus Mustang Panda. Generation 1 embeds FDMTP in Client.dll; Generation 2 (since May 2026) decrypts update.bin. Durable catch: csmonitor.exe side-loading Microsoft.ServiceHosting.Tools.dll and FDMTP custom-protocol C2 over ports 20800-20816.
incidents.action: On any endpoint with QuickFox, update to v3.59.6+ or remove it; block the domains/IPs below and alert on egress to 20800-20816; hunt csmonitor.exe side-loading Microsoft.ServiceHosting.Tools.dll and the update.bin / config.bin artifacts.

iocs.context: Clean build with malicious components removed

incidents.title: CVE-2026-9198 — Langflow unauthenticated RCE mints SUPERUSER tokens
incidents.summary: In Langflow OSS 1.0.0-1.10.0 the /api/v1/auto_login endpoint is neither authenticated nor loopback-bound, so any network caller is issued a SUPERUSER token and can chain a second API endpoint to unauthenticated RCE. It is the first AI-agent platform added to CISA KEV (Aug 4); KEVIntel logged ~650 exploitation attempts from 244 IPs across 41 countries since Jul 6. Durable catch: any external hit to /api/v1/auto_login — Langflow stores model, database and connector credentials, so RCE means full secret exposure.
incidents.action: Upgrade Langflow to the fixed release (patched Jul 17); never expose Langflow to untrusted networks; hunt access logs for /api/v1/auto_login calls from non-loopback sources and rotate every credential/token Langflow was trusted with.

iocs.context: Langflow OSS 1.0.0-1.10.0 code injection — unauth RCE chain
Unauthenticated, non-loopback-bound endpoint that mints SUPERUSER tokens

iocs.value: SUPERUSER token issued to a non-loopback caller

incidents.title: CVE-2026-18577 — N-able N-central auth bypass, RMM-to-endpoint pivot
incidents.summary: An authentication-bypass-via-alternate-path in N-able N-central (an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-18556) hands remote attackers administrative access to the RMM server, then abuse of the built-in Take Control feature to pivot into every managed endpoint. CISA added it to KEV after customer compromises when the first patch proved incomplete. CVSS 8.2. Durable catch: an "MSP Support" admin login, a registered Cloudflared service, and svchost.exe dropped in a user's Documents folder.
incidents.action: Upgrade N-central to 2026.3 HF1; review Take Control activity and admin logins (especially "MSP Support"); block the IPs below; hunt for a Cloudflared service and an svchost.exe under a Documents folder on the N-central server and its managed hosts.

iocs.context: Auth bypass — incomplete patch of CVE-2026-18556; fixed in 2026.3 HF1
Masquerading dropped binary — real svchost never lives here
Legitimate tunnel tool registered as a service for covert access
Default operator account used in the intrusions

incidents.title: CVE-2026-20316 — Cisco Secure FMC static-credential zero-day
incidents.summary: Static, built-in credentials for a low-privilege account in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center let an unauthenticated remote attacker log in and read sensitive data; Cisco rates it High because that foothold chains with other FMC bugs to escalate. Cisco PSIRT observed in-the-wild exploitation during July; there is no workaround, only hotfixes. Reported Jul 29 and carried into this issue — affects FMC 7.0/7.2/7.4/7.6/7.7/10.0, but not Cloud-Delivered FMC.
incidents.action: Apply the Cisco FMC hotfix for your train (7.0-10.0); there is no workaround; audit FMC for logins by the built-in low-privilege account and treat the management plane as critical by restricting its network exposure.

iocs.context: Static built-in low-priv credentials — unauth read access to FMC
No workaround — hotfix only; Cloud-Delivered FMC not affected

iocs.value: Login by the built-in low-privilege FMC account
iocs.context: Chains with other FMC flaws to escalate

incidents.title: CNBackdoor — multi-stage Windows backdoor with scheduled-task persistence
incidents.summary: A multi-component Windows backdoor (Installer_v3500_x64.exe drops InterPartHKIAsync.exe, ioextender.exe and PathMarker.vbs) that stages under %AppData%\Roaming\ExtendedMonitor, persists via an "Extended API 0136301" scheduled task, geolocates the host through public IP checkers, and beacons to tommysbakescodes[.]ws. CYFIRMA published a YARA rule. Durable catch: the ExtendedMonitor folder, the "Extended API 0136301" task, and the tommysbakescodes[.]ws PHP endpoints.
incidents.action: Block tommysbakescodes[.]ws; deploy CYFIRMA's CNBackdoor YARA rule; hunt for %AppData%\Roaming\ExtendedMonitor, the "Extended API 0136301" scheduled task, and the four component filenames below.

incidents.title: KansasGroup ransomware — .kansas4life encryptor
incidents.summary: A newly-observed Windows ransomware that appends .kansas4life to encrypted files and drops a KANSASGROUP.txt ransom note; CYFIRMA flags an uncommon svchost command-line as the execution tell and shipped a Sigma rule. Few network indicators are public yet, so the .kansas4life extension, the KANSASGROUP.txt note, and the anomalous svchost invocation are the reliable catches.
incidents.action: Deploy CYFIRMA's Sigma rule for uncommon svchost command-line parameters; alert on creation of *.kansas4life files and KANSASGROUP.txt notes; keep offline backups and restrict lateral RDP/SMB.
